name: Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa

criteria.description: Presence of generalized mucocutaneous blistering and erosions at or shortly after birth
Immunofluorescence antigen mapping showing cleavage within the lamina lucida of the basement membrane zone
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding laminin-332, type XVII collagen, or integrin subunits
Skin biopsy demonstrating subepidermal blister with cleavage at lamina lucida

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of generalized blistering at birth plus confirmation by immunofluorescence mapping or genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is increasingly used to confirm diagnosis and subtype classification.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Generalized mucocutaneous blistering at lamina lucida level
Mucosal erosions including oral cavity and upper airway

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties
Anemia secondary to chronic blood loss
Respiratory tract infections due to mucosal involvement

rare.symptomName: Squamous cell carcinoma development in chronic wounds

genetic: Pathogenic variants in LAMA3, LAMB3, LAMC2 (laminin-332 genes)
Mutations in COL17A1 (type XVII collagen gene)
Mutations in ITGA6 and ITGB4 (integrin subunits)
other: Immunofluorescence antigen mapping demonstrating cleavage within lamina lucida
Skin biopsy histopathology showing subepidermal blister

distinguishingFeatures: More prominent scarring and milia formation
Mutations in KRT5 or KRT14 genes
Usually milder phenotype with less mucosal involvement

redFlags: Severe generalized blistering at birth with mucosal involvement
Failure to thrive due to feeding difficulties
Recurrent infections and sepsis from skin barrier disruption
references: Fine JD, et al. Inherited epidermolysis bullosa: updated recommendations on diagnosis and classification. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2014.
Uitto J, et al. Epidermolysis bullosa: molecular genetics and clinical phenotype. J Invest Dermatol. 2016.
